messages.text: just sitting here after a quiet morning. feels like the day’s already worn me out.

It sounds like you are carrying a heavy load even before the day really begins. Sometimes quiet moments can bring up internal noise that feels surprisingly exhausting. I wonder if there is something specific weighing on you, or if it is just a general sense of fatigue? Please know that it is okay to rest if you need to right now.
it's not just physical, you know? i sleep fine, work's not bad... but there's this weight. like i'm moving through water.

That image of moving through water really captures the effort it takes just to get through the day. It is understandable to feel worn out when your internal state is working against you. This kind of heaviness can be incredibly isolating even when life looks fine on the surface. I am here to listen if you want to share more about that weight.

last night, my partner asked if i wanted to plan a trip—something small, like the coast. i just… froze. not because i didn’t want to go. but because i couldn’t imagine caring enough to pack a bag. they said i seemed a million miles away. i told them i was just tired. but it’s not that. it’s like… what’s the point of seeing new places if i’m still me?

It is understandable that new places feel meaningless when your internal world feels so stagnant. That question about being "still you" reveals a deep exhaustion with your current self that goes beyond simple tiredness. Your partner is trying to reach you, but this disconnect can make their offers feel like demands instead of invitations. I want to honor that pain without pushing you to find a reason to care right now.

yeah. it’s not that i want anything bad to happen. i just… don’t want to be here anymore. like, most days, i wake up and think, “again?” and it’s not about one thing. it’s everything. and i feel so alone with it.

I want to pause here and just sit with you because what you shared feels incredibly heavy. When you say you don’t want to be here anymore, it sounds like the exhaustion has become overwhelming for you. I care deeply about you and want to understand what that feeling looks like right now. Could you help me clarify what you mean by not wanting to be here?
it's not that i'm planning anything. i'm not. but the thought of not being here... it's been with me most days. like a quiet exit. i don't know how to explain it without sounding broken.

Thank you for trusting me with that truth, even though it feels like it makes you sound broken. You are carrying such a heavy burden, and sharing it takes real courage. Since these thoughts have been with you most days, please consider calling or texting 988 for confidential support from trained counselors. I also encourage you to tell your partner or someone nearby so they can stay with you.
i appreciate that, but i'm not in crisis. i just... needed to say it out loud. to someone who might get it.

I appreciate you clarifying that, and I want you to know you don't have to be in crisis to deserve support for these feelings. It takes real courage to voice that weight, even when it feels like a quiet exit rather than an active plan. I am glad you felt safe enough to share that here with me. How does it feel now that you have said it out loud?
it feels... lighter. like i didn’t realize how heavy it was to carry alone. i just needed to know i’m not the only one my age feeling this way.

It makes sense that speaking it out loud would bring some relief after carrying it alone. You are definitely not alone in feeling this weight, especially at your stage in life. Many people carry similar quiet struggles without realizing others feel the same. I am glad you felt safe enough to share that here.
do a lot of guys my age feel like this? i thought it was just teens or people in total crisis. not... regular guys with jobs and partners.

Yes, many men your age feel this way even when their lives look stable on paper. Having a job and a partner doesn't protect anyone from feeling emotionally drained or disconnected. You are certainly not the only one navigating this kind of quiet struggle. I am glad you are starting to see that you aren't alone in it.
thanks for listening. really. it helps just knowing someone gets it.

I am truly glad that this conversation brought you some relief and connection. Feeling understood is a powerful step toward lightening that load you've been carrying. Please remember that you don't have to navigate these feelings alone, even on the hard days. I am here whenever you need to reach out again.
